sub_graphs.title: EIP-7867: Batch Atomicity Levels
sub_graphs.description: Models the different atomicity guarantees for batch execution

nodes.label: Strict Atomicity Mode
nodes.description: Calls remain atomic even during block reorgs (default)

nodes.label: Loose Atomicity Mode
nodes.description: Atomic only absent reorgs; calls may scatter during reorgs

nodes.label: No Atomicity Mode
nodes.description: Only in-order inclusion guaranteed; calls may interleave

nodes.label: Parse Atomicity Parameter
nodes.description: Extract atomicity level from flowControl request

nodes.label: Check Wallet Atomicity Capability
nodes.description: Verify wallet supports requested atomicity level

nodes.label: Atomicity Level Rejected
nodes.description: Wallet cannot provide requested atomicity guarantee

sub_graphs.description: Models the onFailure behavior modes: rollback, halt, and continue

nodes.label: Call Execution Failed

nodes.label: Check onFailure Mode

nodes.label: Rollback Mode Active
nodes.description: Failed call triggers entire batch revert (default)

nodes.label: Halt Mode Active
nodes.description: Failed call stops execution; subsequent calls skipped

nodes.label: Continue Mode Active
nodes.description: Failed call allows subsequent calls to proceed

nodes.label: Revert Entire Batch
nodes.description: Undo all executed calls in the batch

nodes.label: Stop Batch Execution
nodes.description: Finalize batch with partial execution

nodes.label: Proceed to Next Call
nodes.description: Continue executing remaining calls in batch

ambiguities.text: The specification states calls 'may eventually flip' between success and failure but does not define the conditions under which this occurs
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this refers to reorg scenarios where confirmed transactions may be reverted and re-included with different outcomes

ambiguities.text: 'Loosely atomic calls can experience arbitrary delays' does not specify maximum delay bounds
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume no maximum delay is guaranteed; dapps must implement their own timeout logic at the smart contract level

ambiguities.text: Receipt handling for retried failed calls is not fully specified in terms of which receipt is canonical
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the most recent successful receipt is canonical; failed attempts may have multiple receipts but only final success counts

implicit_assumptions.description: The wallet correctly implements the requested flow control semantics and does not falsely report capabilities
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: DApps could experience unexpected execution outcomes, including loss of funds from improperly handled failures

implicit_assumptions.description: Block reorgs are relatively rare and shallow on the target network
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Loose atomicity mode becomes unreliable; calls may frequently scatter across blocks during deep reorgs

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot force wallet to report false capabilities to manipulate dapp behavior
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious wallets could trick dapps into using weaker atomicity than intended, enabling exploitation

implicit_assumptions.description: DApps encode proper deadlines and timeouts in smart contract logic rather than relying on transaction-level guarantees
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Stale transactions could execute successfully after intended expiration, causing unintended state changes
